How-to guides

Source: vignettes/how-to-guides.Rmd
how-to-guides.Rmd

Task-focused guides for common projr workflows.

1. Initialise a project 

library(projr)

# Interactive prompts (recommended for first-time users)
projr_init_prompt()

# Sensible defaults, no prompts
projr_init()

# Full setup: Git, GitHub, license, citation, renv, etc.
projr_init_all()

This creates _projr.yml, DESCRIPTION, README.md, and directories (_raw_data, _output, _tmp, docs). Git, GitHub, license, and citation setup are optional and prompted or skipped depending on the function used.

# Set license and citation separately
projr_init_license(license = "MIT")
projr_init_cite()

If GitHub credential prompts fail, run projr_instr_auth_github() for setup instructions. Initialisation won’t overwrite existing config files.

You can keep _projr.yml, _projr-<profile>.yml and _projr-local.yml in .projr/config/ as well as the project root. You can split the files between these locations. A root file takes precedence over a nested file with the same name. Configuration updates write back to that file. New files and all relative paths in the configuration start at the project root.

2. Run a development build

Use projr_build_dev() when iterating on code and documents before creating a versioned release.

projr_build_dev()

# Build specific documents only
projr_build_dev(scripts = "analysis.Rmd")
projr_build_dev(scripts = c("methods.Rmd", "results.Rmd"))

On a new project, dev builds stage outputs in _tmp/projr/dev/. Once the project has a version, they use _tmp/projr/v<version>/. Use projr_path_get() to get the output path in development and production builds.

# In your R Markdown or scripts:
fig_path <- projr_path_get("output", "figures", "plot.png")
png(filename = fig_path)
# ... plotting code ...
dev.off()

# Dev build:  _tmp/projr/v0.1.0/output/figures/plot.png
# Final build: _output/figures/plot.png

Hardcoded paths like "_output/plot.png" bypass the cache and write directly to _output during dev builds.

3. Run a final (versioned) build 

# Patch bump (0.1.0 -> 0.1.1) — projr_build() is equivalent
projr_build_patch()

# Minor bump (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0)
projr_build_minor()

# Major bump (0.1.0 -> 1.0.0)
projr_build_major()

A final build clears output directories, renders documents, bumps the version, writes the manifest, uploads to configured destinations, and commits to Git (if configured).

Control output clearing with the PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT env var ("pre", "post", or "never"):

Sys.setenv(PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT = "pre")
projr_build()

Git behaviour is configured in _projr.yml:

build:
  git:
    commit: true
    push: true

4. Archive artefacts

To archive raw data in a shared folder, add a named local destination. For a GitHub release, use a named entry under github instead.

build:
  local:
    backup:
      path: ~/project-archives/study
      content: [raw-data]
  github:
    figures:
      content: [output]
      send:
        cue: if-change

The equivalent R calls are:

projr_yml_dest_add_local("backup", "raw-data", "~/project-archives/study")
projr_yml_dest_add_github("figures", "output", send_cue = "if-change")

Use structure: archive to retain versioned artifacts or structure: latest to keep the current payload. See vignette("configuration") for all the options.

5. Restore artefacts

To reproduce a checked-out production build from its GitHub archive, run projr_restore() inside that checkout. It fills in missing raw data after verifying the recorded file hashes. Use projr_restore(version = "1.2.3") to select a particular build.

# Clone a repo and restore archived content
projr_restore_repo("owner/repo")
projr_restore_repo("owner/repo", path = "~/projects/my-project")

# Restore from the current working directory (already cloned)
projr_content_update()

Restore specific directories:

projr_content_update(label = "raw-data")
projr_content_update(label = c("raw-data", "output"))
projr_content_update(label = "raw-data", type = "local", title = "backup")

By default, projr looks for each label’s configured source, then a build destination containing that label. To reuse a templated archive from an earlier build, pass the concrete path or tag recorded in .projr/BUILDLOG.md as destination.

6. Define directories and labels

The first build writes a starter _projr.yml if the project has no base configuration. On that first build, projr disables Git operations outside a repository and disables pushing in a repository without an upstream. Existing configurations keep their Git settings. You can also create the starter with projr_init(). It declares these paths:

  • raw-data → _raw_data
  • cache → _tmp
  • output → _output
  • docs → docs

Add custom labels in _projr.yml:

directories:
  raw-data:
    path: _raw_data
  raw-data-public:
    path: _raw_data_public
  raw-data-private:
    path: _raw_data_private
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output:
    path: _output
  output-figures:
    path: _output/figures
  docs:
    path: docs

Declare the labels your project uses, with one path per label. A profile can inherit that path from the default configuration. Relative paths start at the project root even when a nested document runs from its own directory. Staging outputs requires a cache label, and rendering documents requires docs. Use safe = FALSE to retrieve a declared final output path.

projr_path_get("raw-data-public")
projr_path_get("output-figures", "plot.png")

7. Use profiles

Profiles let you maintain different configurations for different contexts (development vs production, different machines, etc.).

# Create a profile (creates _projr-dev.yml)
projr_profile_create("dev")

Edit _projr-dev.yml to override specific settings. Unspecified keys fall back to _projr.yml.

build:
  github:
    enabled: false

directories:
  output:
    path: _output_dev

Activate a profile:

Sys.setenv(PROJR_PROFILE = "dev")
projr_build()

# Check active profile
projr_profile_get()

# Delete a profile
projr_profile_delete("dev")

Remember to unset PROJR_PROFILE when switching back to the default configuration.

Keep profile directories out of Git

Suppose raw-data points to lab/measurements in _projr.yml. On a cluster, you keep the data in incoming/assays. Set the latter path in _projr-cluster.yml and give temporary work its own rule.

directories:
  raw-data:
    path: incoming/assays
  cache-scratch:
    path: runs/scratch
    ignore-even-if-inactive: false

Run projr_ignore_auto() to refresh the rules. Git ignores both data directories whichever profile is active. The cluster profile contributes the rule for runs/scratch only while it is active. Paths are literal and relative to the project root. An absolute path contributes a rule only when it lies inside the checkout. An inactive profile can name a drive on another machine without requiring access to it.

ignore-even-if-inactive defaults to true. It extends the directory’s existing ignore, ignore-git, and ignore-rbuild settings across profile switches. Each ignore file includes a path if any contributing profile enables it for that file. projr applies this to .gitignore and, when the project root contains DESCRIPTION, to .Rbuildignore.

If you change raw-data to another path, run projr_ignore_auto(). The next refresh drops the old path’s generated rule as soon as its last qualifying profile reference is removed. Adding a manual ignore to an older project also refreshes its managed rules. Entries above and below the managed section stay in place.

A directory path can also use build placeholders. For example, results/@branch/run-@uuid gives each build its own directory. On branch feature/foo, the branch component is feature_2ffoo. A detached checkout uses __detached- followed by the full commit SHA. @version gives the projr version being built, such as v1.2.3. The UUID is shared with child renders during a build. Outside a build it stays stable for the R session.

A placeholder can occupy an entire component. It also expands before a hyphen, underscore, period, space, or path separator. For example, @version_report.csv expands and @versioned stays literal.

projr writes ignore patterns for the template itself, so another build’s UUID is already covered. A branch placeholder spans a path component in Git’s ignore syntax. Give it a dedicated parent, such as results/@branch, when neighboring source directories should remain trackable.

8. View and manage build logs

Build history is logged to .projr/logs/{dev,output}/history/builds.md. Each build also creates a detailed Quarto log file organised by date.

# View build logs
projr_log_view()

# List detailed log files
list.files(".projr/logs/dev/output",
  recursive = TRUE, pattern = "\\.qmd$"
)

Control logging:

# Disable detailed log files (history still maintained)
Sys.setenv(PROJR_LOG_DETAILED = "FALSE")

# Re-enable
Sys.setenv(PROJR_LOG_DETAILED = "TRUE")

Clear old logs:

projr_log_clear()
projr_log_clear(build_type = "dev")
projr_log_clear(before_date = "2025-01-01")

Logs are never cleared automatically — manage them manually.

9. Query the manifest

Each final build records file hashes in the per-directory histories under .projr/manifests/. Identical directory contents share one file list.

By default, projr hashes files in C++ using one core. To use up to four cores, add the following to _projr.yml or to a profile.

settings:
  hashing:
    approach: cpp
    cores: 4

Set approach: legacy to use the historical R implementation. Both approaches produce the same MD5s at any core count, so changing either setting preserves the directory version for unchanged files.

Compare two versions:

projr_manifest_changes("0.0.1", "0.0.2")
projr_manifest_changes("0.0.1", "0.0.2", label = "output")

Track files across a range of versions:

projr_manifest_range("0.0.1")
projr_manifest_range("0.0.1", "0.0.5", label = "raw-data")

Check when directories last changed:

projr_manifest_last_change()
projr_manifest_last_change("0.0.3")

Practical example — detect raw data changes since a release:

raw_changes <- projr_manifest_changes(
  "0.1.0", projr_version_get(), label = "raw-data"
)
if (nrow(raw_changes) > 0) {
  message("Raw data has changed - outputs may need regeneration")
}

Version strings accept both "0.0.1" and "v0.0.1". All query functions return a 0-row data.frame when there are no results.

10. Configure environment variables

Create environment files at the project root:

file.create("_environment")       # Global defaults
file.create("_environment-dev")   # Profile-specific overrides
file.create("_environment.local") # Machine-specific, git-ignored

Add variables in KEY=value format:

# _environment
PROJR_OUTPUT_LEVEL=std
PROJR_LOG_DETAILED=TRUE

# _environment.local (for secrets — git-ignored)
GITHUB_PAT=your_token_here

Load them:

projr_env_set()

Key variables:

Variable Values Purpose
PROJR_OUTPUT_LEVEL none, std, debug Console verbosity
PROJR_LOG_DETAILED TRUE, FALSE Create detailed log files
PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT pre, post, never When to clear output dirs
PROJR_PROFILE profile name Active configuration profile

See ?projr_env_set and the Environment Variables article for full details.
